36/S0.subgoal: Explain what contextual inquiry is, its active and passive modes, and why the observer must act as an apprentice rather than a teacher.

36/S1.subgoal: Describe the five stages of contextual inquiry and how the reflect stage uses affinity diagrams to analyze observed data.

36/S2.subgoal: Explain how the affinity diagram method organizes contextual inquiry notes into grouped design recommendations, using a note-taking application example, and distinguish those recommendations from implementation.

36/S3.subgoal: Demonstrate how affinity diagram grouping can be applied to calendar app observations to form reminder and scheduling requirement categories.

36/S4.subgoal: Summarize the lecture's coverage of contextual inquiry and affinity diagram analysis, and preview the next part on using the data for implementation.
